title: Signifier
body:
A **signifier** is the perceivable indication that an action is possible. Where an
[[Affordance]] is what the object permits, the signifier is what the user can see about it.

```
underlined blue text       signifies a link
a raised rectangle         signifies a pressable button
a cursor changing shape    signifies that the element under it is interactive
a scrollbar                signifies that there is more content below
a greyed-out control       signifies that the action is currently unavailable
```

Every one of them is a convention that had to be learned, and they work because they are shared
across applications, which is the argument in [[Consistency and Standards]].

The failure mode is removing the signifier while keeping the affordance. Flat design that
strips the border and shadow from a button leaves something clickable that no longer looks
clickable, and the user has to hover over the interface to discover what it does. The reverse
failure is signifying something the system does not offer, such as text styled like a link that
does nothing.

A missing scrollbar is the version that costs the most, since content below the fold with no
indication that it exists is content nobody reads.
